newsitem.title: INDIA: SONY SEES BLACK INK IN INDIA BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: SONY SEES BLACK INK IN INDIA BY 2000.

text.p: Sony Corp's India unit expects to turn profitable by the turn of the century, the head of the company said on Friday.
"We hope to start making profits in three years time when the television market gets to between 3.0 million to 3.5 million units," Yoshio Kubo, managing director, Sony India Pvt Ltd.

Sony India started operations in July 1995 as a fully- owned subsidiary of Japan's Sony Corp. Until now, it has invested $16 million in setting up a 300,000 units a year television assembly facility on the outskirts of New Delhi.

Kubo said Sony India had been slowed by a local television market had not been growing as forecast and was not expected to reach five million by 2000. He added that Sony India had a 12 percent market share in India.
Industry estimates put the television market at a shade over 2.6 million units in 1996/97 (April-March).
Kubo said Sony India's sales were expected to top five billion rupees ($140 million) in 1997/98 (April-March) from 3.45 billion rupees in 1996/97.
